FILEPORTER · QUIET DIRECTION

The transport chamber stripped to the pad, the beam and what you are sending. No rail, no telemetry header, no flank panels — one headline, the destination pads as chips, the payload resting on the deck, and what arrived along the bottom.

All five screens are now at this density and share one language: a 44px light headline, sans labels over mono values, underlined fields instead of boxes, the same floor glow, and the same nav. Mono is reserved for what a machine produced — addresses, fingerprints, sizes, file names.

Click the pad on 01 to run a transport, or drag onto it to arm the field.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE TRANSLATION

Log drops the table chrome and the machine shorthand — Sent and Received instead of arrow glyphs, Verified instead of MATCH. The detail drawer survives: click any received row for Reveal / Copy / Move per item.

Config drops the linked-pads table entirely. It duplicated Pads, and revoke belongs where you look at pads.

Pads presents each device as an object on the floor rather than a card in a grid. A dark pad dims and stops moving.

LIVE ON THESE BOARDS

01 destination chips, click-to-transport, drag-over arming.
02 hover a held pattern for discard.
03 click any received row to open what materialized.
04 every switch and the retention selector; Apply lights when something changes.
First run: Bring this pad online.

Accent hue is a tweak chip on each board.
Sample device names, addresses, fingerprints and transfer figures throughout. Fonts load from Google Fonts, so PNG and PDF export fall back to the local stack.

ALT · THE DENSE CHAMBER

Twenty passes of instrumentation: perspective room, emitter pylons, ceiling recess, wall-mounted readouts, back-wall receiving alcoves, four-phase transport. Kept for reference and for any piece worth pulling forward into 01.
